{{Quote|Doctor, where are you?''"<br />"''Don't be upset with me, Master. If you were a better fighter, we would not be having this conversation.|Grievous and EV-A4-D|audio=DoctorWhereAreYou-LoG.flac|<ref name="decoded" />}}
'''EV-A4-D''', also known as '''A4-D''' or '''Ay-Four-Dee''', was an [[A4 laboratory assistant droid/Legends|A4 laboratory assistant droid]] who served the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] as a [[Medical droid/Legends|medical/repair droid]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. As with many EV-model [[Droid/Legends|droids]], a programming defect caused EV-A4-D to have a sadistic personality. Prior to his work with Grievous, EV-A4-D served as a supervisor in a hospital on the [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Tauber]], but he was relieved from duty after ordering the medical droids under his command to operate on patients without administering painkillers. He was later purchased by the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] and absorbed into the Confederacy.

EV-A4-D was eventually assigned to work as the personal [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]] of Grievous. Stationed in [[Grievous's castle/Legends|Grievous's castle]] on the [[Third moon of Vassek/Legends|third moon of Vassek]], EV-A4-D became the facility's caretaker, managing the general's residence and working to repair any damage he sustained to his cyborg body over the course of the war. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Confederate [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]] [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] [[Mission to Grievous's castle/Legends|lured]] [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] forces to Grievous's castle in order to assess the general's abilities as the [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]]. During the confrontation with the Republic, Grievous was heavily damaged and was repaired by EV-A4-D to be able to confront the intruders once more. EV-A4-D later separated [[Nahdar Vebb/Legends|Nahdar Vebb]] and [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]], the two [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who were leading the Republic forces, allowing Grievous to [[Death/Legends|defeat]] Vebb. However, as EV-A4-D monitored the castle's [[TT-8L gatekeeper droid/Legends|security cameras]] from the control room, he was [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitated]] and destroyed by Fisto.

The droid's body was later recovered by Grievous and reassembled. EV-A4-D then left Vassek, traveling with his master during his military campaigns serving as both doctor and advisor. EV-A4-D was present alongside Grievous during the [[Battle of Dorin|siege]] of [[Dorin/Legends|Dorin]], during which he informed the general of a communication from Count Dooku's [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]], [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]].

==Biography==
===Hospital service===
{{Quote|There may be&hellip;some discomfort.|EV-A4-D|audio=SomeDiscomfort-LoG.flac|<ref name="decoded" />}}
EV-A4-D was manufactured by [[MerenData/Legends|MerenData]] as part of the<ref name="db" /> [[Class one droid/Legends|first-degree]]<ref name="degree">''[[Cynabar's Fantastic Technology: Droids]]'' specifies that [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droids]] are [[Class one droid/Legends|class one droid]]s.</ref> [[EV-series supervisor droid/Legends|EV-series supervisor droid]] line.<ref name="db" /> Like most of the EV-series, A4-D,<ref name="decoded" /> or Ay-Four-Dee,<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|3|A4-D (Ay-Four-Dee)}}</ref> was affected by a programming defect during production that caused him to have a sadistic and malicious personality.<ref name="decoded" /> Regardless of the defect, MerenData sold the EV-series [[Droid/Legends|droids]], and EV-A4-D became a supervisor to the droids serving as the staff in a hospital on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tauber]]. EV-A4-D's work in the hospital yielded dramatically higher productivity from the droids; however, the supervisor droid's methods disturbed the [[Human/Legends|Human]] doctors. After serving in the hospital for a time, EV-A4-D ordered the droids to operate on the patients without the use of painkillers. As a result, EV-A4-D was returned to MerenData, only to be later purchased by the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]].<ref name="db" />

===The general's doctor===
{{Quote|Sometimes I wonder why you submitted to the changes.''"<br />"''Improvements! I submit to no one. I ''chose'' them. Now get on with it.|A4-D and General Grievous|audio=ISubmitToNoOne-LoG.flac|<ref name="decoded" />}}
[[File:EV-A4-D_works_on_Grievous.png|thumb|left|300px|EV-A4-D works to repair Grievous's body.]]
During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the InterGalactic Banking Clan allied itself with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a separatist government opposing the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="db ibc">{{DB|organization|igbc|InterGalactic Banking Clan}}</ref> EV-A4-D, modified with medical and repair attachments, was assigned to work in the [[Grievous's castle/Legends|castle]] of [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] Confederate [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]], on the [[Third moon of Vassek/Legends|third moon]] of the planet [[Vassek/Legends|Vassek]]. There, EV-A4-D served as a repair droid and doctor to Grievous.<ref name="db" /> Aside from his duties as Grievous's personal physician, EV-A4-D also acted as the caretaker of the Vassek facility, overseeing its day-to-day maintenance, managing the general's [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuard]] [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], and feeding [[Gor/Legends|Gor]], Grievous's pet [[Roggwart/Legends|roggwart]].<ref name="Visual Guide Ultimate Battles">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Visual Guide: Ultimate Battles]]''</ref> The general was fond of Gor, but believed his abilities as the castle guardian could be improved. As such, Grievous enlisted the aid of EV-A4-D in attaching cybernetic limbs, exoskeletal plates, and [[Armor/Legends|armor]] to the roggwart.<ref name="TCWCE">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Over the course of the war, EV-A4-D grew used to his master returning from the battlefront in need of repair, and at one point he was aware of the reasons behind Grievous's transformation from a proud [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]] warrior into a cyborg subordinate of Confederate [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]] [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]. This information was eventually erased from his memory.<ref name="Visual Guide Ultimate Battles" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] member [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] was [[Mission to Rodia/Legends|captured]] by Republic forces after a failed attempt to bring [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]] into the Confederacy.<ref name="Cloak of Darkness">{{TCW|Cloak of Darkness}}</ref> Shortly after his capture, Gunray [[Rescue on the Tranquility/Legends|escaped]] from captivity aboard and fled in a stolen [[Consular-class cruiser (Charger c70 retrofit)/Legends|Republic frigate]]. Gunray's escape presented Dooku with an opportunity to reassess Grievous's abilities to lead the Droid Army, which had been called into doubt after a recent string of defeats. While Grievous was away from his castle, Dooku planted the [[Homing beacon/Legends|homing beacon]] of Gunray's [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]] within the general's lair, and he also remotely deactivated Grievous's IG-100 MagnaGuards, leaving EV-A4-D to believe that Grievous himself had deactivated them.<ref name="LoG" />

====Intruders====
{{Quote|Wait&hellip;where's the other Jedi? Oh, no&hellip;|EV-A4-D's final words|audio=EVA4DLastWords-LoG.flac|<ref name="decoded" />}}
[[File:EV-A4-D.png|thumb|right|280px|EV-A4-D monitors Kit Fisto and Nahdar Vebb within Grievous's castle.]]
Following the placement of the tracking beacon, [[High Jedi General/Legends|High Jedi General]] [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Nahdar Vebb/Legends|Nahdar Vebb]] arrived on the third moon of Vassek with a small force of Republic [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], having tracked down the Republic frigate in the hopes of recapturing Gunray. Dooku and Gunray revealed their manipulations to the Republic forces via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]], leaving the Jedi to plan the capture of Grievous instead of Gunray. The group resolved to take Grievous into custody upon his arrival at his castle. When he returned to his lair, Grievous was ambushed by the Republic forces. In the following [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]], Fisto severed the general's legs with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], and Grievous's faceplate was damaged by [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire.<ref name="LoG" />

The general escaped into the castle's control room, where he was met by EV-A4-D, who reprimanded him for allowing the Jedi to damage him, and informed Grievous of his guards' deactivation. EV-A4-D left and began preparations for repairing the cyborg, while Grievous remained in the control room to release Gor, whom he hoped would be able to kill the intruders. However, Grievous was pulled away from watching Gor's efforts by EV-A4-D, who was ready to take Grievous in for repairs. In the castle's operating theater, EV-A4-D began removing Grievous's damaged parts, replacing his severed legs with new limbs and painfully lifting away the general's faceplate in order to place a new one on.<ref name="LoG" />

After completing Grievous's repairs, EV-A4-D followed the general back to the control room, informed Grievous of an incoming transmission from Dooku, at which point Grievous learned of Dooku's deception. This, coupled with the Jedi's defeat of Gor, spurned Grievous into hunting down the Jedi himself, despite EV-A4-D's insistence that he take time to rest. While Grievous left to combat Vebb and Fisto, EV-A4-D remained within the control room to monitor the castle's [[TT-8L gatekeeper droid/Legends|security cameras]]. Upon catching sight of the Jedi attempting to enter the control room, EV-A4-D alerted Grievous via the stronghold's speaker system.<ref name="LoG" />

Fisto opened the entrance to the control room, but Vebb insisted upon remaining outside to confront Grievous. While the two Jedi argued about their course of action, EV-A4-D resealed the entry to the control room, locking Fisto within and leaving Vebb outside to engage Grievous on his own. EV-A4-D gleefully watched Grievous gain the upper hand in his duel with Vebb and encouraged the general to kill the Jedi. However, the droid forgot about Fisto, realizing too late that he was now locked in the control room with the Jedi. Fisto approached EV-A4-D from behind and destroyed the droid by [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitating]] him through the control room chair with his lightsaber. Shortly after EV-A4-D's destruction, Grievous killed Vebb, but Fisto was able to escape.<ref name="LoG" />

====Rebuilt====
{{Quote|Ah, but you are not me, Doctor, for I am the leader of the most powerful droid army the galaxy has ever seen, and you are a simple servant droid!''"<br />"''Doctor and advisor.''"<br />"''I tire of your comical wit. Do not make me regret having you reassembled.|Grievous and EV-A4-D argue during the Battle of Dorin|<ref name="LaPR Prelude" />}}
Following the Jedi's escape, Grievous found EV-A4-D's destroyed body and had the droid reconstructed. Once repaired, EV-A4-D left Vassek's moon with his master, no longer relegated solely to housekeeping and repair work. In addition to his position as Grievous's doctor, the droid became an advisor to the cyborg, and accompanied him during his time away from the Vassek castle. EV-A4-D was present during Grievous's [[Battle of Dorin|attack]] on the [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dor]] [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Dorin/Legends|Dorin]] in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]], during which the cyborg general attempted to exterminate the native population.<ref name="LaPR Prelude" />

In the latter stage of Grievous's initial assault, EV-A4-D informed the general of an incoming transmission from [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], a Confederate commander and [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolyte]] apprentice of Count Dooku's. Although Grievous was unwilling to accept the communication, EV-A4-D convinced him to listen to Ventress, who was relaying a message from Dooku himself. Ventress warned the general of a Republic fleet that had departed [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and was headed to reinforce the natives of Dorin and explained that the fleet was under the command of [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who could easily turn the tide of battle. Grievous was undeterred by the information, and ordered EV-A4-D to begin preparations for the arrival of the Republic fleet.<ref name="LaPR Prelude" />

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Master, the armor patches are getting cold, and contrary to your belief, I do have other things to do.|EV-A4-D, to General Grievous|audio=OtherThingsToDo-LoG.flac|<ref name="decoded" />}}
[[File:EV-A4-Dtools-LoG.png|thumb|left|280px|EV-A4-D with his vast array of attachments deployed]]
Similar to other EV-series supervisor droids from MerenData,<ref name="negd">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> EV-A4-D displayed a cruel personality.<ref name="decoded" /> While successful in increasing the productivity and efficiency of the medical droids working on Tauber, EV-A4-D's practices concerned the organic doctors he worked with. His methods eventually led to his dismissal when he ordered the medical droids to refuse painkillers to the hospital's patients, causing needless pain for the individuals that the hospital meant to help.<ref name="db" />

With the transfer to Grievous's Vassek castle, EV-A4-D's high-level abilities as a supervisor and taskmaster went unused, as his responsibilities were limited to housekeeping and the management of a small force of MagnaGuards. EV-A4-D grew bored with his work and wished for excitement&mdash;a wish that was granted with the arrival of Fisto and Vebb. Although normally highly attentive, EV-A4-D became careless during the intrusion, losing track of Fisto and realizing only too late that the Jedi was directly behind him, prepared to strike.<ref name="Visual Guide Ultimate Battles" />

During his service to Grievous as the cyborg general's personal doctor, EV-A4-D developed an uncommon relationship with his patient. Although normally unwilling to tolerate insolence or disrespect, Grievous endured the droid's criticism of his abilities and demands during repairs. Although A4-D worked diligently to ensure quality repairs,<ref name="Log Commentary">{{SW|url=video/lair-of-grievous-episode-featurette|text="Lair of Grievous" Episode Featurette}}</ref> the droid enjoyed the opportunity to inflict pain upon the Kaleesh during his [[Reconstructive surgery/Legends|reconstructive surgeries]].<ref name="CWC 6.25">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.25|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.25]]</ref> EV-A4-D was curious of the reasons behind Grievous's physical transformation<ref name="Log Commentary" /> and took care in ensuring his work on the mechanical body would not go to waste, insisting that Grievous take time to rest after his repairs. The droid was delighted at Grievous's prowess during his duel with Vebb, cheering him on moments before he was bisected by Fisto's attack.<ref name="LoG" />

While most of EV-A4-D's<ref name="Visual Guide Ultimate Battles" /> [[Color/Legends|bronze]]-colored<ref name="LoG" /> body resembled that of other EV-series droids, EV-A4-D possessed modifications that allowed him to serve as Grievous's doctor. A small attachment that hung over one of EV-A4-D's<ref name="Visual Guide Ultimate Battles" /> white<ref name="LoG" /> [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] housed his logic center. Several arms that were attached to his torso and back had medical instruments affixed to the ends, while one of EV-A4-D's primary upper limbs was affixed with a "carousel arm" that allowed for rotation at the wrist between a surgical [[Laser/Legends|laser]] and a precision gripper. Circulatory fluid used during surgical operations hung from a limb extending from the droid's back. EV-A4-D also had a supply palette attached to his waist and magnetized feet.<ref name="Visual Guide Ultimate Battles" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Conception===
{{Quote|The scenes in "Lair of Grievous" between me (as Grievous) and A4-D were fun. I want more interaction with that character. I like the idea of someone who can boss Grievous around while looking out for him.|Matthew Wood|<ref name="SayWat">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20090312.html|text=Say Wat? Matthew Wood Talks Tambor}}</ref>}}
EV-A4-D was created for the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' series,<ref name="LoG" /> appearing in the tenth episode of its [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]], "[[Lair of Grievous]]," which aired on [[December 12]], [[2008]];<ref name="Lair of Grievous Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode010.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Lair of Grievous}}</ref> however, at the time of the episode's original air date, EV-A4-D was known simply as "A4-D." The droid's full name was not revealed until the episode's [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars#The Clone Wars: Decoded|''Decoded'']] re-airing, which also introduced EV-A4-D's backstory as a hospital supervisor.<ref name="decoded" />

The droid was created when Series Director [[Dave Filoni]] expressed his interest in having [[Matthew Wood]], the voice of General Grievous, and sound designer [[David Acord]] perform in a scene together. The episode's writers decided to have Acord play Grievous's mouthy doctor droid. Wood, Filoni, and Acord brainstormed together on what the droid would sound like, hoping to find a speech pattern as far from Grievous's as possible. Acord eventually settled on the distinctive speaking style of the late [[Wikipedia:Paul Lynde|Paul Lynde]].<ref name="DVD Featurette">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season One|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season One]]&mdash;Featurette 110: Lair of Grievous</ref> Wood stated the scenes between EV-A4-D and Grievous were fun to record. Wood analyzed the character as someone who could "boss Grievous around," all while looking out for the general.<ref name="SayWat" />

In the [[2009]] [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season One|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season One]] DVD featurette for "Lair of Grievous", Filoni expresses his regret for killing off EV-A4-D at the end of the episode. The director indicates that he would be interested in bringing back the droid as a disembodied head carried around by Grievous in future episodes of the series.<ref name="DVD Featurette" /> Indeed, Wood expressed an interest in having more interactions between Grievous and EV-A4-D in the series.<ref name="SayWat" /> EV-A4-D did eventually make a return to the series, albeit not in an episode, but rather a [https://web.archive.org/web/20110629021855/http://www.starwars.com/theclonewars/news20091103fd/index.html script] presented at the Star Wars Fan Days III convention that served as a prelude to the [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] episode, "[[Landing at Point Rain]]."<ref name="LaPR Prelude" />

===Inconsistencies and non-canon material===
In the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Season One Episode Guide, Part One|Season One Episode Guide]] included in the [[Star Wars Insider 106|106th issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine<ref name="Insider 106">{{InsiderCite|106|Star Wars: The Clone Wars Season One Episode Guide, Part One|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Season One Episode Guide, Part One}}</ref>—published [[December 17]], [[2008]]<ref name="Insider 105">[[Star Wars Insider 105|''Star Wars Insider'' 105]]</ref>&mdash; EV-A4-D is incorrectly labeled as [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R6-H5/Legends|R6-H5]].<ref name="Insider 106" /> The ''[[Galaxy at War]]'' sourcebook from [[Wizards of the Coast]] contradicts the "Lair of Grievous" decoded episode by stating that the droid is named A-4D and is an [[A4 laboratory assistant droid/Legends|A-Series medical droid]].<ref name="GAW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> This article assumes that ''Galaxy at War'' is in error.

EV-A4-D is featured in [[The Clone Wars Animated Comics|''The Clone Wars'' Animated Comics]], a series of short, non-[[canon]] videos based on [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] products. In Episode 4: ''A Grievous situation'', A4-D accompanies General Grievous to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where the cyborg was shot down during a [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfight]] over the planet by Jedi Master [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]]. While the general sunbathed in the desert's twin suns, EV-A4-D worked to reattach the limbs his master lost in the crash. The droid was unable to do so before the arrival of Republic forces, resulting in Grievous's arms falling off his body when he attempted to duel Nahdar Vebb. Grievous carries EV-A4-D off-screen, where the droid quickly finishes his repairs so that the general can return to his duel. Grievous is forced to retreat when Koon arrives to provide support to Vebb, but leaves EV-A4-D behind with the Republic forces. This video was available on the LEGO Star Wars website, and features the option to view the story from either the Republic or Confederate perspective.<ref name="Lego">{{LEGOWeb|subdomain=starwars|url=en-us/Comics/Player/2010-4.aspx|text="A Grievous Situation"|nolive=1}}</ref>

EV-A4-D also appears in the [[2011]] non-canon video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]'', in which he appears in the game's adaptation of "Lair of Grievous." His role as Grievous' repair droid is humorously portrayed, as A4-D forces the droid General to take a spoonful of medicine. After the completion of this mission in the [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]] version, A4-D is also unlocked for use in the Free Play mode of the game.<ref name="LSWIII">''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]''</ref>
